newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania elects its president until the year 2000.
newsitem.headline: Romania elects its president until the year 2000.

text.p: Romanian voters will elect their president on Sunday in a decisive run-off after throwing out of government ex-communists who had run the country since 1989.
Here are some key facts and figures on the election.

More than 17 million Romanians aged 18 and above must choose between incumbent Ion Iliescu and his centrist rival, Emil Constantinescu, the two best-placed contenders after the opening round earlier this month.
Constantinescu of the opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) bloc is supported by all major parties and by ex-prime minister Petre Roman, who was third in the opening round.
The CDR has signed a governing coalition accord with Roman's Social Democratic Union.

Iliescu's Party of Social Democracy (PDSR), descendants of pre-1989 ruling communists, lost to the CDR in parliamentary elections and is going into opposition for the first time in the post-Communist era.
Iliescu and Constantinescu ran against each other in Romania's 1992 elections, in which Iliescu decisively defeated Constantinescu, 62 percent to 39 percent.
In Romania's first post-Communist election two years earlier, Iliescu collected 85 percent of the vote.
But the president held only a four percentage point advantage over his rival in the first round of this year's election -- 32 percent to 28 percent -- and faces a tough race on Sunday.
The sole opinion poll issued ahead of the vote showed Constantinescu ahead 53 percent to 47 percent, but surveys here tend to be unreliable.
The candidate winning the most votes is declared elected, regardless of the turnout.
The country's 15,177 polling stations will open from 6 a.m. (0400 GMT) to 9 p.m. (1900 GMT), but voting can be extended until midnight (2200 GMT) if election authorities feel more time is needed.

Five local watchdog groups are fielding some 14,000 local observers to watch over polling stations, amid accusations from both sides of dirty tricks. International observers are also being accredited.
Two polling institutes have said they will announce the results of exit polls as soon as voting ends. They gave contradictory forecasts after the opening round.

Election authorities have limited resources to cope with Romania's poor communications and say returns from 43 regional centres will not be collated until late on Monday. Official results will be announced by Wednesday, November 20.
Iliescu has held power since the December 1989 overthrow and execution of Stalinist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu in eastern Europe's bloodiest anti-communist revolt.
